title: Annotatio V §.IV cont. close: denying Oral ≠ denying presence or sacramental; stop mid-§.IV before §.6
pass_a_gloss: To the Second and Third I may finish with one and the same response — namely that each fails in Consequence: For (1) From negation of the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body, who will ever attempt a progress to negation of the substantial Presence of His Body in the Supper? What will become of the Spiritual non-Sacramental Eating of John 6, by which mediating yet Christ whole is so present to us that He dwells in our Hearts (Gal. 3)? Whither will the omnipresence of Christ’s Body go whenever we abstain from Oral Eating or use of the Eucharistic Sacrament? Although the very omnipresence of Christ’s Body is in more than one way hostile to His Eating — i.e. to Reception of Christ’s Body into the mouth: For how will you receive into the mouth what by the force of its omnipresence is already then in the Mouth? And how will you lead away by teeth to throat and stomach what you so ate with the Mouth that yet it was most present to all parts of the eater’s Body at the same moment of time? (2) Nor will a better nexus meet one proceeding from Negation of Oral Eating to Negation of Sacramental, seeing that Spiritual Eating also is a part of Sacramental Eating, and so for Luther himself — and I do not doubt for all Lutherans — the chief and principal. But from a denied less principal part of Sacramental Eating to the denied Sacramental whole or universal, a gaping consequence will be given. Nor is there reason for A. to fear that yet thus every distinction between Sacramental and Spiritual Eating is removed if Oral Eating of Christ’s Body is exiled from the Sacred Supper: For Sacramental Eating forever stands apart from Spiritual by this evident distinction — that Spiritual is bare and destitute of bread-eating; but Sacramental always enjoys this bread-eating as essentially belonging to it; Spiritual is never Oral except in the Supper’s Sacrament; and then it is Oral of the blessed bread only, not of Christ’s Body; Sacramental conversely always exists as Oral — namely of the blessed bread — even when it remains severed from the spiritual Eating of Christ’s Body.
pass_b_english: Reply to (2)–(3): consequence fails. Denying Oral does not deny substantial presence — witness spiritual non-sacramental eating (Jn 6; Christ dwelling in hearts). Omnipresence itself sits oddly with ‘receiving into the mouth what is already in the mouth.’

Nor does denying Oral deny sacramental eating: spiritual is the chief part of sacramental for Luther; denying a lesser part is not denying the whole. Distinction remains — spiritual bare of bread; sacramental always has blessed-bread oral, even when severed from spiritual eating of the Body. Stop mid-§.IV before §.6 / further Anti-Irenicum.
source_text: Ad Secundum & Tertium responsione unâ eâdemque defungi mihi licet, utrumque scil. Consequentia deficere: Enimverò (1) À negatione Oralis Manducationis Corporis Christi, quis unquam ad negationem Præsentiæ Corporis ejus in Cœna substantialis, progressum molietur? Quid fiet de Manducatione Spirituali non Sacramentali Joh. 6. quâ tamen mediante, Christus totus ita nobis præsens est, ut habitet in Cordibus nostris Gal. 3? Quorsum evadet omnipræsentia Corporis Christi, quandocunque Orali Manducatione, seu Sacramenti Eucharistici usu, abstinemus? Quanquam ipsa omnipræsentia Corporis Christi, Manducationi ejus, i. e. Receptioni Corporis Christi in os, non unô modô inimica sit: Quî enim receperis in os, quod vi omnipræsentiæ suæ, jam tum in Ore est? Et quomodo dentibus gutturi & stomacho subduces, quod ita Ore manducasti, ut omnibus tamen manducantis Corporis partibus, eodem temporis momento præsentissimum fuerit? (2) Nec melior obveniet nexus procedenti à Negatione Oralis Manducationis, ad Negationem Sacramentalis, quandoquidem etiam Spiritualis Manducatio, Manducationis Sacramentalis pars est, eóque Luthero ipsi, nec dubito, Lutheranís omnibus, præcipua & principalis. At verò à negatâ Manducationis Sacramentalis parte minus principali, ad negatam Sacramentalem totam vel universam, hiulca dabitur consequentia. Nec est, quod metuat A. sublatum tamen sic omne inter Sacramentalem & Spiritualem Manducationem, discrimen esse, si Oralis Corporis Christi Manducatio, S. Cœnâ exulet: Nam Sacramentalis Manducatio, à Spirituali, hôc evidenti discrimine, in perpetuum distat, ut Spiritualis nuda sit panisque manducatione destituatur; Sacramentalis verò hac panis manducatione semper gaudeat, ceu essentialiter sibi competente, Spiritualis nunquam Oralis sit, nisi in Sacramento Cœnæ; Sit verò tùm Oralis, benedicti tantùm panis, non Corporis Christi; Sacramentalis vice versâ, semper Oralis existat, panis scil. benedicti, etiam tùm cùm à spirituali Corporis Christi Manducatione sejuncta manet.
notes: Reply to 2–3: presence/sacramental remain; mid-§.IV stop.
